Implement 3 residual data-safety fixes in /opt/nxeon/worker/migrate-real.ts (Nxeon migration engine), and migrate-detect.ts only if detection needs it. After editing run `cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsc --noEmit` until CLEAN (exit 0) and `cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsx --test test/migrate-consolidate.test.ts` (green). Do NOT run the worker, deploy, or commit. Read the relevant regions first. Report per-fix final line numbers. Refuse-and-name when unsure; never make a migration less safe.

Context: host-native Postgres/MySQL are already dumped consistently (`pg_dumpall`, `mysqldump --single-transaction`) — find that path (search `mysqldump`, `pg_dumpall`, dbEngines, the dump streaming `onSource(...) > ${work}/dumps/...` and the import). Containerized DBs are handled by F1 (search `dbEngineInfo`, `containerDbDumpScript`, `restoreVolumes`). A `MIGRATE_OVERWRITE_TARGET_DATA` flag (`OVERWRITE_TARGET_DATA`) already exists and guards DB import clobber — reuse it for F-A12. The source read-only guard is CATASTROPHIC-only (rm/mv/dd of block devices), so `mongodump`/`redis-cli`/`mysqldump --lock-tables` are fine (pure reads/locks, no data writes).

## FIX F4 — host-native Mongo & Redis: consistent dump + honest-refuse fallback
Today only host mysql/postgres get logical dumps; a host-native MongoDB (`/var/lib/mongodb`) or Redis (`/var/lib/redis`) is migrated only if the operator hand-picks its datadir → a hot file copy of a live WiredTiger/RDB/AOF = torn/stale. Add, mirroring the existing host mysql/postgres dump→restore path:
- Detect a host-native Mongo (mongod running / `/var/lib/mongodb` present / port 27017 host-native) and Redis (redis-server running / `/var/lib/redis` / port 6379 host-native). You may need a small detection add in migrate-detect.ts (mirror how host mysql/postgres presence is detected ~537) OR detect at apply-time via `onSource` probes — pick whichever matches the existing pattern with least churn.
- Mongo: if `mongodump` exists on the source, `onSource(mongodump --archive)` (+ auth flags only if the source mongo requires auth — detect cheaply; default no-auth for a host mongo) streamed to `${work}/dumps/host-mongo.archive`; restore on target after mongod is up via `mongorestore --archive --drop`. Ensure the target has mongodb-org / mongo tools or install/skip gracefully.
- Redis: trigger a consistent snapshot read-only — `redis-cli BGSAVE` then copy the resulting `dump.rdb` (or `redis-cli --rdb -` streamed) to the target's redis datadir before redis starts; OR if AOF, note it. 
- HONEST-REFUSE fallback: if the dump tool is absent or auth is needed and unknown, do NOT silently hot-copy a live datadir as if consistent — push an honest step naming the DB and that it needs a manual dump. 
- Also: add `redis` and `mongo` to the empty-datadir refuse/stateful set if they aren't already (the audit noted Redis was excluded), so an empty redis/mongo volume for a DB we intend to restore is handled like the SQL engines.

## FIX F5 — MyISAM safety in the host mysqldump
`mysqldump --single-transaction` is consistent for InnoDB ONLY; MyISAM tables tear under writes. Detect whether the source has non-InnoDB tables (query information_schema for ENGINE != InnoDB, read-only) and, when present, use a consistent path for them (`--lock-tables` or `--lock-all-tables`, or dump those tables separately with a lock) instead of relying solely on `--single-transaction`. If you can't determine engines cheaply, at minimum add `--single-transaction --quick` and push a note that MyISAM tables (if any) were copied without a lock. Keep InnoDB behavior unchanged (no added downtime for the common case).

## FIX A12 — file-overwrite protection on a non-fresh target (reuse MIGRATE_OVERWRITE_TARGET_DATA)
The file/tree rsync merges into the SAME paths on the target (OS dirs are already protected by UNSAFE_PREFIXES/UNSAFE_EXACT). On a NON-fresh target, a customer's existing files at an app path (e.g. /var/www/site) can be overwritten silently. Add a guard using the existing `OVERWRITE_TARGET_DATA` flag: before copying a source tree to a target path, if the target path ALREADY EXISTS and is non-empty AND is not one we just created for this migration AND the flag is false → push an honest step naming the path ("the new server already has files at <path>; not overwriting — set MIGRATE_OVERWRITE_TARGET_DATA=1 to replace, or migrate to a fresh server") and SKIP that tree; if the flag is true, proceed (log overwrite). Be careful and conservative: don't false-positive on a path the migration itself created earlier in the same run, and don't block the common fresh-target case (empty/absent target path → proceed as today). Keep the existing behavior when the flag is set.

## Constraints
- Reuse existing helpers (dump streaming, onSource, import, report/push, the stateful regex). Validate interpolated values; single-quoted `sh -c '…'`; secrets never in argv/logs.
- Do NOT regress F1/F2/F3/A1 or any container/compose/web/units work already in the file.
- Finish only when tsc is clean AND the consolidate test passes. Report per-fix final line numbers, how F4 detects+dumps mongo/redis, and how A12 decides "non-fresh target path".

## How F4 detects + dumps Mongo/Redis
- **Detect** (apply-time `onSource` probes, no detect-file change): host-native Mongo = `mongod` on the host PATH **or** `/var/lib/mongodb` exists; host-native Redis = `redis-server` on PATH **or** `/var/lib/redis` exists. A containerised Mongo/Redis has neither on the host, so F1's container path isn't double-handled.
- **Mongo dump/restore**: if `mongodump` is present, `onSource("mongodump --archive")` streams to `${work}/dumps/host-mongo.archive` (default no-auth; on auth-required the dump comes back empty/errored → honest-refuse, never a hot copy). Restore ensures `mongorestore`+`mongod` on the target (best-effort install since Mongo isn't in stock apt; if still absent, keep the dump and refuse), then `mongorestore --archive --drop`.
- **Redis snapshot/restore**: cheap `redis-cli PING` liveness/auth probe (non-`PONG`/`NOAUTH` → honest-refuse); on success `onSource("redis-cli --rdb -")` streams a consistent RDB (pure read, works for AOF servers too) to `${work}/dumps/host-redis.rdb`; target `redis-server` installed from stock apt, Redis stopped, RDB placed at `/var/lib/redis/dump.rdb` (owner `redis:redis`), Redis restarted to load it.
- Both restores are additionally guarded by `OVERWRITE_TARGET_DATA` (A1-style) if the target already holds Mongo/Redis data.

## How A12 decides "non-fresh target path"
Before copying source tree `p` to its content path `dst` (`dst === p` unless remapped), it probes the target: the path counts as non-fresh if it's a directory containing at least one entry (`find dst -mindepth 1 -print -quit`) or a non-directory that exists — **and** `dst` is not in `createdThisRun` (paths this run already populated, so a remap's freshly-`mkdir`'d empty dir and multi-path merges never false-positive). Non-fresh + flag off → honest step naming the path and SKIP; non-fresh + flag on → log overwrite and proceed; empty/absent (every fresh-server migration) → unchanged.

One judgment call worth flagging: adding `redis` to the container empty-volume refuse set means a redis container whose volume didn't migrate will now hard-refuse to start (previously a warn-and-start) — this is the safer behavior the audit asked for, but it will change behavior for pure-cache redis containers with a genuinely empty volume.
